long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Alexandria, Saban moved with his family to Israel at 12 and began in music as a bass player and concert promoter. After relocating to France, he built a privately owned record label, then moved to Los Angeles and supplied music for television. That progression gave him both the rights experience and production base for a shift into children's programming.

Through the Saban Family Foundation, he and his wife have supported medical, educational and children's programs in the United States and Israel. Their gift led Children's Hospital Los Angeles to rename its pediatric research institute for the family. He currently serves as a non-executive director of Universal Music Group.

proposed_details.existing_value: Haim Saban is an Israeli-American media proprietor, investor, and producer of records, film, and television. A businessman with interests in financial services, entertainment, and media, and an estimated net worth of $2.8 billion, he is ranked by Forbes as the 232nd richest person in America. Saban is the founder of Saban Entertainment, producer and distributor of children's television programs in the US such as Power Rangers. He headed up consortiums which purchased the broadcasters ProSiebenSat.1 Media and Univision Communications. He is a major donor to the United States Democratic Party and active in pro-Israel political efforts in the United States. In March 2017, Saban was honored with the 2,605th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame for his achievements in television.
